question: Why must you avoid scrubbing the skin too hard when washing off chemical contaminants?

options.A: It can break the skin barrier and increase toxin absorption
options.B: It wastes too much clean water in the emergency ward
options.C: It makes the chemical change into a stronger poison
options.D: It stops the soap from creating enough foam

explanation: Damaging the outer layer of the skin opens up pathways for chemicals to enter the bloodstream much faster. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T6#BMP110_U7_T6_h3)

question: Which of the following parameters is NOT recorded in the fetal condition section of the partograph?

options.A: Fetal heart rate
options.B: Amniotic fluid status
options.C: Maternal blood pressure
options.D: Degree of skull molding

explanation: Maternal blood pressure belongs to the maternal condition section, while heart rate and liquor status belong to the fetal section. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T6#BMP212_U2_T6_h2)

question: A pregnant woman in labour is resting in bed. Which side-lying posture is most appropriate to prevent supine hypotension syndrome?

options.A: Lateral position
options.B: Trendelenburg position
options.C: Prone position
options.D: Supine position

explanation: The lateral position removes the weight of the gravid uterus off the major blood vessels in the abdomen, ensuring good blood return to the heart. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T8#BMP110_U4_T8_h2)

question: A patient with long-term liver disease has a swollen belly and tiny, spider-like red blood vessels visible on the chest. What is this skin finding called?

options.A: Keloid scars
options.B: Purpuric spots
options.C: Spider angiomas
options.D: Butterfly rash

explanation: Spider angiomas are small, widened blood vessels on the skin surface caused by how the body handles hormones when the liver is damaged. [learn more](BMP125_U4_T2#BMP125_U4_T2_h4)

question: In which layer of the skin do you find the secretory coils of sweat glands?

options.A: Basal layer
options.B: Dermis
options.C: Epidermis
options.D: Hypodermis

explanation: Sweat glands are tubular structures with their secretory coils located within the dermal layer of the skin. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T11#BMP111_U4_T11_h1)

question: A nursing mother asks why her underarm sweat has a stronger smell than sweat on her arms. Which gland is responsible?

options.A: Subcutaneous fat cells
options.B: Eccrine sweat glands
options.C: Apocrine sweat glands
options.D: Sebaceous oil glands

explanation: Apocrine glands produce thicker secretions in areas like the armpits, which develop odors when skin bacteria break them down. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T7#BMP111_U4_T7_h2)

question: What is the tiny space between two communicating neurons called?

options.A: Dendritic cleft
options.B: Axon hillock
options.C: Synaptic cleft
options.D: Myelin gap

explanation: The synaptic cleft is the microscopic gap between the end of one neuron and the start of the next cell. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T5#BMP121_U5_T5_h6)

question: Which size of intravenous cannula is best for quickly replacing fluids during a heavy PPH?

options.A: Central line of any size
options.B: Small-bore 22G or 24G
options.C: Midline catheter of 20G
options.D: Large-bore 16G or 18G

explanation: Large-bore cannulas allow fluids and blood to flow in quickly when a mother is bleeding heavily. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T2#BMP315_U2_T2_h2)

question: What is the main way aminoquinoline drugs fight malaria parasites?

options.A: Stopping the parasite from entering red blood cells
options.B: Binding directly to human hemoglobin molecules
options.C: Preventing the parasite from detoxifying harmful heme
options.D: Destroying the reproductive organs of adult protozoa

explanation: These drugs stop the parasite from getting rid of toxic waste from digesting blood, poisoning the parasite with its own waste. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T11#BMP124_U4_T11_h2)

question: Why do skeletal muscle fibers have multiple nuclei inside a single cell?

options.A: They form during development by the fusion of many smaller embryonic cells.
options.B: They require extra nuclear control because they lack mitochondria.
options.C: They must constantly divide by mitosis to repair minor daily tears.
options.D: They absorb nuclei from nearby fat cells to increase their energy storage.

explanation: During early development, many smaller cells fuse together to form one long muscle fiber, which is why there are multiple nuclei in a single cell. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T4#BMP111_U3_T4_h2)

question: What is the typical electrical charge inside a resting neuron?

options.A: Negative seventy millivolts
options.B: Positive seventy millivolts
options.C: Positive forty millivolts
options.D: Zero millivolts

explanation: When a neuron is at rest, its internal charge sits at about -70 mV, making the inside more negative than the outside. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T5#BMP121_U5_T5_h2)

question: Why do epithelial tissues rely on nearby connective tissues for nourishment?

options.A: Their cells are too tightly packed to allow blood flow
options.B: They are completely avascular without blood vessels
options.C: They produce constant secretions that wash away blood
options.D: Their cell junctions block all internal fluid movement

explanation: Epithelial tissue contains no blood vessels of its own, so cells receive oxygen and nutrients through diffusion from neighboring tissues. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T6#BMP111_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which physical finding should alert the nurse to potential heart failure in an endocarditis patient?

options.A: Dark lines beneath the fingernail beds
options.B: Small red spots on the palms of the hands
options.C: Crackles or rales in the lung bases
options.D: Painful red bumps on the fingertips

explanation: Fluid backing up into the lungs due to failing heart valves creates crackles or rales, signaling developing heart failure. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T7#BMP125_U2_T7_h7)

question: Which physiological change during pregnancy directly affects how the body processes medications?

options.A: Increased blood volume and altered kidney filtration
options.B: The total elimination of gastric acid production
options.C: A complete shutdown of all liver enzyme functions
options.D: Decreased heart rate throughout all three trimesters

explanation: Pregnancy causes major hemodynamic shifts, including higher blood volume and changes in renal clearance, which alter drug distribution and elimination. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T1#BMP124_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which action verb fits a learning objective at the evaluating level of Bloom's taxonomy?

options.A: List
options.B: State
options.C: Define
options.D: Critique

explanation: Critique requires making judgments based on criteria, which fits the evaluating tier. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T2#BMP312_U3_T2_h7)

question: Which management function involves looking ahead to set goals and decide future actions?

options.A: Staffing
options.B: Directing
options.C: Controlling
options.D: Planning

explanation: Planning is specifically the proactive phase where managers establish objectives and map out the steps required to achieve them. [learn more](BMP312_U1_T5#BMP312_U1_T5_h2)

question: A woman develops a severe uterine infection after an unsterile abortion, with rapid shock and dark red urine. Which organism is most likely responsible?

options.A: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.B: Clostridium perfringens
options.C: Staphylococcus aureus
options.D: Candida albicans

explanation: Clostridium perfringens produces toxins in uterine tissue, causing severe tissue destruction, red blood cell breakdown, and rapid shock. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T8#BMP116_U2_T8_h4)

question: A pregnant woman asks if she should double her food intake because she is eating for two. What is the best response?

options.A: She only needs a modest increase in calories, focusing on nutrient-dense local foods rather than double portions
options.B: She must double every meal to ensure the baby grows twice as fast
options.C: She should cut back on food to avoid gestational diabetes
options.D: She only needs extra food during the first trimester

explanation: The body becomes more efficient during pregnancy, so a massive increase in food quantity is unnecessary. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T16#BMP212_U1_T16_h2)

question: Which protein makes up thick myofilaments?

options.A: Actin
options.B: Myosin
options.C: Troponin
options.D: Tropomyosin

explanation: Thick filaments are built from bundled molecules of the protein myosin. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T1#BMP111_U3_T1_h3)

question: When applying international research findings to a local Nigerian clinic, what must a midwife consider?

options.A: Whether the original researchers speak the local language
options.B: Whether local resources and patient contexts match the study
options.C: If the research paper has colorful pictures and charts
options.D: How many awards the primary author won for the study

explanation: Evidence must fit the local clinical setting, staff capacity, and available supplies before it can be safely adopted. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T4#BMP225_U4_T4_h5)

question: A frightened laboring woman needs an emergency Caesarean section but refuses to sign the consent form out of panic. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Ask a relative to sign the form without informing the patient
options.B: Cancel the procedure and allow her to attempt a spontaneous vaginal birth
options.C: Provide calm reassurance and briefly explain the life-saving reason for the surgery
options.D: Proceed with the surgery immediately without any form of consent

explanation: Calm communication helps ease panic, allowing the patient to understand the emergency and give informed consent. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h2)

question: In the nursing process, what is the main goal of the implementation phase?

options.A: To evaluate long-term recovery rates
options.B: To formulate specific patient diagnoses
options.C: To carry out planned nursing interventions
options.D: To collect initial baseline health data

explanation: Implementation is the action phase where you put the planned care into motion. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T5#BMP120_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which condition is NOT directly caused by long-term calcium loss in mothers?

options.A: Maternal bone mineral loss
options.B: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: Osteopenia
options.D: Osteoporosis

explanation: Gestational diabetes is related to blood sugar and insulin, whereas calcium depletion directly affects bone density conditions like osteopenia and osteoporosis. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T6#BMP118_U2_T6_h5)

question: Which hormone tells the kidneys to hold onto sodium and get rid of potassium?

options.A: Adrenaline
options.B: Aldosterone
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Cortisol

explanation: Aldosterone is made by the outer part of the adrenal glands and helps the kidneys balance fluids and electrolytes. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T2#BMP121_U4_T2_h4)

question: When is ECT typically considered for a patient with a mental health condition?

options.A: Before trying any talk therapy or medication
options.B: When other standard treatments have failed
options.C: Only when the patient requests outpatient therapy
options.D: As the very first step in routine counseling

explanation: Medical teams usually reserve ECT for severe cases where medications and talk therapy have not provided relief. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T5#BMP223_U4_T5_h1)

question: How do you search for postpartum hemorrhage while excluding caesarean sections?

options.A: postpartum hemorrhage NOT caesarean section
options.B: postpartum hemorrhage OR caesarean section
options.C: postpartum hemorrhage AND caesarean section
options.D: postpartum hemorrhage WITH caesarean section

explanation: Using the NOT operator allows the researcher to filter out studies that focus on the excluded term. [learn more](BMP123_U4_T2#BMP123_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary benefit of using closed-loop communication during a resuscitation?

options.A: It allows the team to work completely in silence
options.B: It replaces the need to document events in the case note
options.C: It confirms that instructions were clearly heard and understood
options.D: It prevents doctors from speaking to midwives at all

explanation: Repeating an order back ensures the person executing it caught every detail correctly, reducing dangerous medical errors. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T4#BMP324_U1_T4_h5)

question: What imaging tool is considered the gold standard for diagnosing osteoporosis by measuring bone mineral density?

options.A: Dual-energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DXA) scan
options.B: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)
options.C: Routine abdominal X-ray plate
options.D: Standard pelvic ultrasound scan

explanation: The DXA scan measures bone density safely and accurately at key skeletal sites like the hip and spine. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T18#BMP111_U2_T18_h4)

question: Which bacterium is most commonly linked to acute bacterial tonsillitis (strep throat)?

options.A: Escherichia coli
options.B: Staphylococcus aureus
options.C: Group A beta-hemolytic Streptococcus
options.D: Pseudomonas aeruginosa

explanation: Infections caused by Group A beta-hemolytic Streptococcus are the most frequent bacterial cause of acute tonsillitis requiring antibiotics. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T4#BMP111_U6_T4_h4)

question: A patient has white patches in the mouth that bleed slightly when scraped. What condition is this?

options.A: Oral candidiasis
options.B: Gingival hyperplasia
options.C: Normal tongue coating
options.D: Dental caries

explanation: White patches resembling curdled milk that bleed when removed are a classic sign of a fungal infection called oral thrush or candidiasis. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T3#BMP110_U5_T3_h2)

question: What is the term for sending a patient from a primary health clinic to a General Hospital due to a complication?

options.A: Upward referral
options.B: Community outreach
options.C: Downward discharge
options.D: Lateral transfer

explanation: Moving a patient from a lower level of care to a higher, more specialized facility is known as an upward referral. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T3#BMP110_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is NOT a typical complication linked to maternal overnutrition during pregnancy?

options.A: Obstructed labor from a large baby
options.B: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: Severe irreversible bone marrow failure
options.D: Pregnancy-induced hypertension

explanation: Overnutrition leads to metabolic and mechanical pregnancy complications like diabetes and high blood pressure, not bone marrow failure. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T1#BMP118_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why does a normal pregnancy make a woman more prone to rapid clotting issues?

options.A: The body naturally increases clotting factors to protect against bleeding
options.B: The liver stops producing proteins during active labor
options.C: Blood volume decreases significantly during the third trimester
options.D: Platelet counts drop to zero right before delivery

explanation: Pregnancy is a high-clotting state by design, meaning the blood clots more easily to safeguard against blood loss during birth. [learn more](BMP311_U4_T6#BMP311_U4_T6_h1)

question: What common duty do family members often take on during a patient's hospital stay in Nigeria?

options.A: Providing bedside care, cooking, and supporting daily needs
options.B: Auditing the hospital financial accounts daily
options.C: Prescribing medications to the patient
options.D: Performing major surgical procedures in the ward

explanation: Family members in many Nigerian hospitals actively assist with physical care, feeding, and supplying daily necessities. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T6#BMP110_U2_T6_h3)

question: What physical sign indicates that a uterine perforation with peritonitis has likely occurred?

options.A: Painless swelling of the lower extremities
options.B: Rigid, tender abdomen with guarding
options.C: Complete absence of any vaginal discharge
options.D: Elevated blood pressure and flushed skin

explanation: Peritonitis causes the abdominal wall muscles to become tight and rigid, accompanied by severe tenderness when touched. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T3#BMP320_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why is a secondary immune response so much faster than a primary response?

options.A: Pre-existing memory cells instantly recognize and react to the antigen
options.B: Bone marrow creates brand new white blood cells instantly
options.C: The pathogen becomes weaker every time it enters the human body
options.D: Innate barriers disappear completely after the first infection occurs

explanation: Memory cells left over from the first exposure allow the immune system to skip the slow initial activation steps. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T6#BMP111_U6_T6_h7)

question: You measure a pregnant woman's blood pressure before giving a prescribed antihypertensive drug. What is this action called?

options.A: Routine drug stock inventory
options.B: Pre-administration assessment
options.C: Aseptic drug preparation
options.D: Post-medication documentation

explanation: Checking baseline parameters like blood pressure before giving a drug ensures it is safe to proceed with that dose. [learn more](BMP120_U2_T1#BMP120_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why do patients with HHS typically not develop severe ketoacidosis?

options.A: Patient diets lack any dietary fat components
options.B: High blood osmolality destroys all body acids
options.C: Residual insulin prevents significant fat breakdown
options.D: The kidneys rapidly excrete all produced ketones

explanation: Even a small amount of remaining insulin stops the breakdown of fats, preventing large amounts of ketones from forming. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T4#BMP216_U2_T4_h2)

question: Why would a midwife choose a qualitative approach when studying maternal nutrition?

options.A: To calculate the exact body mass index of every pregnant woman
options.B: To measure the exact weight of food consumed daily in grams
options.C: To uncover cultural beliefs and personal reasons behind food choices
options.D: To determine the statistical probability of a deficiency disease

explanation: Qualitative methods help researchers understand the personal and cultural factors that shape how people eat and live. [learn more](BMP225_U1_T3#BMP225_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why should educators avoid trick questions or confusing wording in midwifery exams?

options.A: They make the grading guide too hard to calculate
options.B: They test reading confusion instead of actual clinical knowledge
options.C: They stop students from finishing the exam within one hour
options.D: They take too long to type on a standard computer

explanation: Trick questions measure a student's ability to decipher confusing English rather than their understanding of midwifery. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T9#BMP312_U3_T9_h5)

question: Which simple habit helps protect individuals from catching hookworm infections?

options.A: Wearing protective footwear outdoors
options.B: Avoiding all contact with sunlight
options.C: Sleeping under insecticide nets
options.D: Boiling all drinking water twice

explanation: Since hookworm larvae live in damp soil and penetrate bare skin, wearing shoes acts as an important barrier. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T10#BMP124_U4_T10_h6)

question: Why is observing vomit part of a full physical check in midwifery?

options.A: It shows she is taking iron pills
options.B: It gives direct clues about upper digestive health
options.C: It tells the exact age of the pregnancy
options.D: It replaces checking blood pressure

explanation: Vomit acts as a physical sample of what is happening inside the upper gut when problems arise. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T5#BMP110_U6_T5_h1)

question: Which sign best indicates that a grieving mother has reached acceptance?

options.A: She insists her baby is hidden in the ward
options.B: She speaks about her loss with calm sorrow and plans for the future
options.C: She directs insults at the nursing staff
options.D: She refuses to speak and cries at every sound

explanation: Reaching acceptance allows individuals to process sorrow constructively and look ahead. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T3#BMP120_U5_T3_h6)

question: What type of antibodies will be found in the plasma of a person with blood group A?

options.A: Both anti-A and anti-B
options.B: Anti-B antibodies
options.C: Anti-A antibodies
options.D: No antibodies at all

explanation: People with blood group A have A antigens on their cells, so their immune system naturally develops antibodies against the B antigen. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T6#BMP111_U5_T6_h2)

question: A midwife sees thick green meconium in the amniotic fluid as the baby's head crowns. What is the most important first step?

options.A: Give oral oxytocin to speed up the birth
options.B: Ask the mother to stop pushing and rest for two hours
options.C: Get equipment and team ready for possible newborn resuscitation
options.D: Do an immediate instrumental delivery before checking vitals

explanation: Thick meconium can mean the baby experienced stress and might breathe in fluid, so being ready to care for the newborn right away is essential. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T1#BMP212_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why do rows of hash marks like ##### suddenly appear inside a spreadsheet cell?

options.A: The data file has been locked by a user
options.B: The formula contains a mathematical error
options.C: The column is too narrow to show the number
options.D: The computer has a serious virus infection

explanation: Hash marks indicate that the cell value is wider than the current column width allows. [learn more](BMP123_U3_T2#BMP123_U3_T2_h3)

question: What does the term "brain drain" refer to in the context of Nigerian tertiary health care?

options.A: The closure of university medical schools due to protests
options.B: The mass emigration of skilled healthcare professionals abroad
options.C: The removal of outdated books from hospital libraries
options.D: A medical condition caused by severe mental exhaustion

explanation: Brain drain describes the loss of trained doctors, nurses, and midwives who leave the country for better opportunities overseas. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T4#BMP110_U2_T4_h8)

question: Why is a spinal block preferred over an epidural for an emergency Caesarean section that needs to happen immediately?

options.A: It lets the mother walk around the theatre room
options.B: It completely avoids all risks of low blood pressure
options.C: It does not require any sterile equipment
options.D: It works much faster than an epidural

explanation: Spine medication goes straight into the spinal fluid, producing surgical numbness in minutes compared to the slower onset of an epidural. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T8#BMP213_U2_T8_h2)

question: What is the standard adult dose of ergometrine given by injection in routine midwifery practice?

options.A: 200 milligrams
options.B: 2.0 milligrams
options.C: 20 milligrams
options.D: 0.2 milligrams

explanation: The standard therapeutic dose for an adult injection is 0.2 mg, which is equal to 200 micrograms. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T2#BMP213_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why do the mother's kidneys have to work harder during pregnancy?

options.A: To process waste from both the mother and the baby
options.B: To increase blood pressure for the placenta
options.C: To prevent the bladder from shrinking
options.D: To stop all protein from leaving in the urine

explanation: The maternal kidneys take on extra work to clear out waste products from the growing baby along with the mother's own waste. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T6#BMP212_U1_T6_h1)

question: What structure are sebaceous glands typically attached to in the skin?

options.A: Blood capillaries
options.B: Sweat ducts
options.C: Hair follicles
options.D: Nerve endings

explanation: Most sebaceous glands connect directly to hair follicles to discharge their oily secretions onto the hair shaft and skin surface. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T10#BMP111_U4_T10_h1)

question: Which condition is classified as a major obstetric emergency requiring instant action?

options.A: Itchy skin during the third trimester
options.B: Mild lower back pain at term
options.C: Postpartum haemorrhage
options.D: Normal painless Braxton Hicks contractions

explanation: Postpartum haemorrhage involves heavy bleeding after delivery that can quickly lead to maternal death if ignored. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T1#BMP110_U7_T1_h5)

question: Why does physiological hemodilution occur in pregnant women?

options.A: Red blood cells are actively destroyed by the placenta
options.B: Excessive water drinking dilutes the salt in the blood
options.C: The body stops producing bone marrow cells temporarily
options.D: Plasma increases much faster than red blood cells

explanation: Because plasma volume expands much more rapidly than red blood cell mass, the blood becomes diluted, leading to a lower reading on hemoglobin tests. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T4#BMP212_U1_T4_h2)

question: What essential emergency drug must be nearby before giving morphine?

options.A: Naloxone
options.B: Adrenaline
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Magnesium sulfate

explanation: Naloxone is the specific opioid antagonist used to reverse dangerous respiratory depression caused by morphine. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T1#BMP124_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why does a pregnant woman's cardiac output increase significantly?

options.A: To fight off potential infections common in the female reproductive tract
options.B: To handle the large increase in circulating blood volume needed for the baby
options.C: To prevent the mother's blood pressure from dropping to dangerous levels
options.D: To compensate for the weakening of the maternal heart valves caused by hormones

explanation: Pregnancy causes blood volume to expand so the placenta gets enough blood, meaning the heart has to pump more each minute. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T12#BMP111_U5_T12_h7)

question: Which symptom points most clearly toward a life-threatening anaphylactic reaction?

options.A: A mild headache lasting for several hours
options.B: Dark discoloration of the urine
options.C: Swelling of the airway and severe difficulty breathing
options.D: Mild constipation after taking iron tablets

explanation: Airway compromise and breathing difficulty are hallmarks of anaphylaxis, making respiratory support the top priority in emergency management. [learn more](BMP120_U2_T7#BMP120_U2_T7_h3)

question: Why must midwives consider local resource availability when choosing care actions?

options.A: To eliminate all documentation requirements in the hospital
options.B: To replace the need for physical assessments during labor
options.C: To ensure the planned actions are realistic and can be performed
options.D: To reduce the total number of patients admitted to the ward

explanation: An intervention is useless if the clinic lacks the supplies, water, or equipment required to carry it out safely. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T4#BMP120_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which item must be removed from the patient before they are transferred to the operating theatre?

options.A: Underwear made of cotton
options.B: Dentures and metal jewelry
options.C: Surgical site markings
options.D: Identification wristbands

explanation: Dentures can dislodge and block the airway during intubation, and metal jewelry can cause burns if electrocautery is used. [learn more](BMP120_U4_T1#BMP120_U4_T1_h6)

question: What does the term 'lead time' mean in the context of hospital supply requisition?

options.A: The time it takes for an ordered supply to arrive from the central store
options.B: The number of hours a midwife works before taking a break
options.C: The period between a pregnant woman arriving and delivering her baby
options.D: The duration a sterile instrument pack can sit safely on a shelf

explanation: Lead time measures the delay between submitting a requisition form and actually receiving the items on the ward. [learn more](BMP312_U2_T2#BMP312_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which substance serves as the primary energy source for the developing fetus?

options.A: Calcium
options.B: Albumin
options.C: Folic acid
options.D: Glucose

explanation: Glucose crosses the placenta readily to supply constant energy for fetal metabolism and overall growth. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T2#BMP210_U5_T2_h3)

question: Which part of an open sterile drape or field is safely considered non-sterile?

options.A: The exact center of the tray
options.B: The bottom layer resting on the table
options.C: The outer one-inch border
options.D: The metallic handles of the forceps

explanation: The edges are easily touched or compromised during handling, so the outer margin is always treated as contaminated. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T3#BMP120_U3_T3_h3)

question: Which drug is the safest and most effective first choice for routine AMTSL?

options.A: Misoprostol
options.B: Magnesium sulfate
options.C: Ergometrine
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Oxytocin is preferred because it works quickly and has very few side effects for healthy mothers. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T5#BMP212_U3_T5_h2)

question: Which of the following is classified as a flat bone?

options.A: Humerus
options.B: Femur
options.C: Scapula
options.D: Calcaneus

explanation: The shoulder blade, or scapula, is a classic example of a flat bone located in the appendicular skeleton. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T5#BMP111_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why is colostrum often called the baby's first immunization?

options.A: It acts as a strong pain reliever for newborns
options.B: It builds the bone structure of the infant
options.C: It contains high amounts of protective antibodies
options.D: It provides all the daily iron the baby needs

explanation: Colostrum is packed with immunoglobulins like IgA that line the gut and protect against invading pathogens. [learn more](BMP118_U3_T2#BMP118_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which of these is a classic sign of emotional or spiritual distress in a terminally ill patient?

options.A: Interest in hospital paperwork
options.B: A sudden increase in daily appetite
options.C: Deep restlessness and open expressions of fear
options.D: A stable heart rate and normal blood pressure

options.B: Closing the clinic temporarily until the farming season comes to a complete end
options.C: Meeting with women and village leaders to reschedule clinics to market days or evenings
options.D: Handing out heavy financial fines to families who fail to attend morning clinic

explanation: Collaborating with the community to adapt clinic schedules to their livelihood demonstrates practical problem-solving based on local needs. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T4#BMP117_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the eight bones that make up the neurocranium?

options.A: Frontal
options.B: Maxilla
options.C: Occipital
options.D: Sphenoid

explanation: The maxilla is a facial bone belonging to the viscerocranium, not the neurocranium. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T7#BMP111_U2_T7_h2)

question: Where does the growing uterus push the stomach during pregnancy?

options.A: Upward and slightly to the left
options.B: Backward against the spinal column
options.C: Forward through the abdominal wall
options.D: Downward into the pelvic cavity

explanation: As the uterus grows, it physically displaces the stomach upward and to the left of its normal position. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T7#BMP212_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical consequence of severe portal hypertension?

options.A: Development of swollen esophageal varices
options.B: Permanent closure of the main renal arteries
options.C: Risk of life-threatening gastrointestinal bleeding
options.D: Formation of alternative collateral blood pathways

explanation: Portal hypertension causes blood to back up into collateral veins, creating varices and bleeding risks, but it does not directly close the renal arteries. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T19#BMP111_U5_T19_h5)

question: Which substance must bind to Vitamin B12 in the stomach to enable its absorption further down the gut?

options.A: Pepsinogen
options.B: Intrinsic factor
options.C: Bile salts
options.D: Hydrochloric acid

explanation: Intrinsic factor is produced by cells in the stomach and is required for Vitamin B12 absorption further down the tract. [learn more](BMP121_U2_T3#BMP121_U2_T3_h5)

question: What clinical sign strongly suggests that a patient with cholecystitis has a burst gallbladder and generalized peritonitis?

options.A: Frequent passing of pale, foul-smelling liquid stools
options.B: Rigid, board-like abdomen with severe rebound tenderness
options.C: Sudden appearance of bright yellow jaundice in the eyes
options.D: A drop in body temperature to below normal levels

explanation: When the gallbladder bursts and spills infected bile into the abdominal cavity, the lining becomes extremely irritated, causing the abdominal muscles to tense up rigidly. [learn more](BMP125_U4_T4#BMP125_U4_T4_h6)

question: A postpartum mother taking an alpha-blocker feels dizzy when she stands up quickly. What is the best advice to give her?

options.A: Rise slowly from a sitting or lying position
options.B: Exercise vigorously to boost circulation
options.C: Stop taking the prescribed medication immediately
options.D: Drink extra cups of coffee

explanation: Dizziness upon standing is caused by blood pressure dropping when blood vessels dilate. Changing positions gradually helps prevent this. [learn more](BMP124_U2_T3#BMP124_U2_T3_h7)

question: What happens to the stored lipids in adipocytes during periods of fasting or starvation?

options.A: They evaporate through the pores of the epidermis
options.B: They transform permanently into water molecules
options.C: They turn directly into rigid bone tissue
options.D: They are broken down to supply metabolic energy

explanation: The body mobilizes stored fat reserves from the hypodermis to provide necessary calories when food intake is insufficient. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T3#BMP111_U4_T3_h3)

question: How do mood swings typically show up in a woman experiencing maternity blues?

options.A: She remains permanently sad and completely unresponsive
options.B: She shows total apathy and refuses to hold her baby
options.C: She shifts rapidly between happiness and sudden crying
options.D: She displays unprovoked anger toward every visitor

explanation: Lability means the mood is changeable; mothers often laugh one minute and cry the next over minor matters. [learn more](BMP223_U2_T1#BMP223_U2_T1_h3)

question: What defines an open fracture?

options.A: The bone shatters into multiple small pieces
options.B: The fracture heals without any medical help
options.C: The broken bone breaks through the skin
options.D: The bone is cracked only on one side

explanation: An open fracture happens when the broken bone pushes through the skin to the outside. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T5#BMP110_U7_T5_h3)

question: Why are generic textbook care plans discouraged in clinical practice?

options.A: They prevent doctors from prescribing necessary medical treatments
options.B: They take too much time to read during emergency obstetric situations
options.C: They fail to address the unique cultural and physical needs of the individual
options.D: They are legally forbidden by the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: Every pregnant woman has distinct personal and clinical needs that require tailored rather than generic interventions. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T4#BMP120_U1_T4_h5)

question: What does the ductus arteriosus turn into after permanent tissue changes take place?

options.A: Ligamentum arteriosum
options.B: Medial umbilical ligament
options.C: Ligamentum venosum
options.D: Ligamentum teres

explanation: After the ductus arteriosus stops carrying blood, its muscular walls shrink and turn into a fibrous band called the ligamentum arteriosum. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T5#BMP210_U5_T5_h5)

question: A 62-year-old market trader undergoes a DXA scan, and her report reveals a lumbar spine T-score of -2.8. How should this result be interpreted?

options.A: It confirms the complete absence of bone cells
options.B: It shows mild osteopenia without fracture risk
options.C: It indicates the presence of osteoporosis
options.D: It represents completely normal bone density

explanation: A T-score of -2.5 or lower meets the diagnostic threshold for osteoporosis, indicating significant bone mineral loss. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T18#BMP111_U2_T18_h4)

question: Which two structures join together to form each ejaculatory duct?

options.A: Ureter and urinary bladder neck
options.B: Testis and epididymal head
options.C: Bulbourethral gland and prostate
options.D: Vas deferens and seminal vesicle duct

explanation: The duct from the seminal vesicle merges with the vas deferens to create the ejaculatory duct. [learn more](BMP210_U3_T2#BMP210_U3_T2_h5)

question: What is a common sign that a patient is not getting good quality sleep?

options.A: Patient reports feeling unrefreshed and tired during the day
options.B: Patient's blood pressure drops below normal limits
options.C: Patient develops visible swelling in the lower extremities
options.D: Patient has an elevated white blood cell count on lab work

explanation: Daytime tiredness and feeling exhausted after waking are signs of poor sleep quality that patients report directly. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T9#BMP110_U4_T9_h2)

question: What defines asymptomatic bacteriuria in an expectant mother?

options.A: Presence of bacteria in the urine without clinical symptoms of infection
options.B: Inability to pass urine despite a full bladder
options.C: Frequent painful urination accompanied by high fever
options.D: Severe lower abdominal pain with blood in the urine

explanation: Asymptomatic bacteriuria means bacteria are multiplying in the urine, but the woman feels completely fine and has no typical urinary symptoms. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T10#BMP221_U4_T10_h2)

question: A patient has an open fracture with the bone sticking out. What is the correct initial action regarding the bone?

options.A: Pull the limb firmly to straighten the bone out
options.B: Push the bone gently back inside before splinting
options.C: Leave the bone alone and cover it with a clean dressing
options.D: Wash the exposed bone thoroughly with tap water

explanation: Never push an exposed bone back inside, as this increases the risk of a severe infection. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T5#BMP110_U7_T5_h5)

question: You finish making an unoccupied bed for a postpartum mother who is currently walking in the hallway. What final safety action should you take?

options.A: Pull all the top covers tightly to the very top of the frame
options.B: Leave the wheels unlocked so staff can move it easily
options.C: Raise the bed to its highest level so it is ready for use
options.D: Leave the bed in a low position with the wheels locked

explanation: Leaving an empty bed in the lowest position with locked wheels ensures patient safety when they return and attempt to get back in. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T2#BMP110_U4_T2_h4)

question: Which of the following does NOT drive antimicrobial resistance in the community?

options.A: Purchasing leftover drugs without a professional prescription
options.B: Sharing remaining medications among family members
options.C: Completing the full prescribed dosage of antibiotics
options.D: Using broad-spectrum agents for simple viral infections

explanation: Finishing a prescribed drug course clears the infection completely. Stopping early or misusing drugs is what actually drives resistance. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T1#BMP124_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which cranial nerve supplies motor movement to all the muscles of facial expression?

options.A: Cranial nerve V
options.B: Cranial nerve VII
options.C: Cranial nerve X
options.D: Cranial nerve III

explanation: The facial nerve controls all the superficial muscles responsible for facial movements and expressions. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T7#BMP111_U3_T7_h2)

question: Why is moving a patient prematurely without preparation dangerous?

options.A: It can worsen the patient's existing condition during the journey
options.B: It always causes the transport vehicle to break down on the road
options.C: It increases the cost of fuel for the health facility
options.D: It prevents the receiving doctor from writing prescriptions

explanation: Unstable patients who are rushed without stabilization often deteriorate rapidly once movement and vibrations begin. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T11#BMP110_U7_T11_h1)

question: How does the coverage of cephalosporins generally change as generations advance from first to third?

options.A: Activity becomes restricted to anaerobic fungi
options.B: Gram-negative coverage increases
options.C: Gram-positive coverage increases exclusively
options.D: All bacterial coverage disappears entirely

explanation: As cephalosporin generations get newer, they generally become more effective against gram-negative bacteria, helping to treat tougher infections. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T3#BMP124_U4_T3_h2)

question: What does a test for fecal occult blood primarily screen for?

options.A: Excessive dietary fat malabsorption
options.B: Hidden bleeding within the gastrointestinal tract
options.C: Specific bacterial infections causing diarrhea
options.D: The presence of common intestinal parasites

explanation: Occult blood tests detect microscopic amounts of blood in the stool that are not visible to the naked eye. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T1#BMP125_U3_T1_h6)

question: Besides internal storage, where else does heart muscle get calcium to trigger contraction?

options.A: Breakdown of glycogen granules stored within the sarcoplasm
options.B: Active transport pumps located on the outer nuclear membrane
options.C: Extracellular fluid entering through channels in the cell membrane
options.D: Direct absorption from the red blood cells flowing inside the chamber

explanation: Heart tissue relies heavily on calcium entering from outside the cell to help trigger internal muscle contraction. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T3#BMP111_U3_T3_h4)

question: Chronic hypertension in pregnancy means high blood pressure was identified before which gestational week?

options.A: 20 weeks
options.B: 12 weeks
options.C: 28 weeks
options.D: 34 weeks

explanation: The 20-week threshold separates high blood pressure that started before pregnancy from new conditions arising later in gestation. [learn more](BMP221_U3_T1#BMP221_U3_T1_h4)

question: Convert a doctor's order of 0.5 grams into milligrams for proper administration.

options.A: 0.05 milligrams
options.B: 50 milligrams
options.C: 500 milligrams
options.D: 5,000 milligrams

explanation: To convert grams to milligrams, multiply by 1,000, which moves the decimal point three places to the right. [learn more](BMP120_U2_T6#BMP120_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is the main protein produced by skin cells that gives skin its strength and toughness?

options.A: Elastin
options.B: Melanin
options.C: Keratin
options.D: Collagen

explanation: Keratin is a tough, fibrous protein that protects underlying tissues from physical and chemical damage. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T1#BMP111_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the name of the specialized chart used to monitor the progress of active labor and maternal-fetal well-being?

options.A: Partograph
options.B: Temperature sheet
options.C: Prescription chart
options.D: Antenatal card

explanation: The partograph provides a pictorial overview of labor progress, helping clinicians spot prolonged labor or distress early. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T1#BMP218_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary function of elastic fibers in connective tissue?

options.A: Allowing tissues to stretch and return to their original shape
options.B: Anchoring epithelial cells tightly to the underlying basement membrane
options.C: Forming a rigid supportive framework inside solid organs
options.D: Providing maximum resistance against heavy compressive loads

explanation: Elastic fibers contain the protein elastin, which gives structures like blood vessels and lung tissue the ability to recoil after stretching. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T7#BMP111_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the main smooth muscle that forms the wall of the urinary bladder?

options.A: Detrusor muscle
options.B: Sphincter muscle
options.C: Pudendal muscle
options.D: Trigone muscle

explanation: The detrusor muscle is the primary smooth muscle of the bladder wall. It stretches as the bladder fills and contracts to push urine out during voiding. [learn more](BMP121_U3_T5#BMP121_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why do midwives often prefer a vaginal exam over an ultrasound during active labor?

options.A: It provides a clear visual image of the internal pelvic organs on a screen
options.B: It completely eliminates the risk of introducing bacteria into the uterus
options.C: It gives immediate physical feel of cervical opening and baby descent
options.D: It is completely painless for every woman

explanation: Direct physical touch allows the midwife to quickly feel the cervix and the baby right at the bedside. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T5#BMP211_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is the main goal when a surgeon chooses the level for an amputation?

options.A: To completely eliminate all post-surgery pain
options.B: To shorten the duration of the surgical operation
options.C: To preserve maximum length and joint function
options.D: To prevent the need for any future wound dressings

explanation: Surgeons carefully choose the amputation level to save as much of the limb and joint as possible, which helps the patient use a prosthesis much easier later. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T8#BMP216_U3_T8_h1)

question: A researcher assigns pregnant women to receive a new malaria prevention drug or standard care by flipping a coin. Which core characteristic of an experiment does this represent?

options.A: Blinding
options.B: Manipulation
options.C: Stratification
options.D: Randomization

explanation: Flipping a coin assigns participants purely by chance, which is the definition of randomization. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T4#BMP225_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which chemical messenger is released at the neuromuscular junction to stimulate muscle fibers?

options.A: Acetylcholine
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Myosin
options.D: Lactic acid

explanation: Acetylcholine is released from motor neurons to cross over and stimulate the muscle fiber membrane. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T1#BMP111_U3_T1_h5)

question: How can a midwife quickly check if a wrapped instrument tray has been through an autoclave cycle?

options.A: By looking at the colour change on the external chemical indicator tape
options.B: By checking the weight of the metal container on a weighing scale
options.C: By smelling the interior wrapping paper for a distinct chemical scent
options.D: By feeling the temperature of the metallic package with bare hands

explanation: Chemical indicator tape changes colour when exposed to the proper sterilization heat parameters. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T2#BMP116_U5_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary foundation of health promotion and disease prevention in Nigeria?

options.A: Tertiary teaching hospitals
options.B: International health grants
options.C: Primary healthcare
options.D: Private specialist clinics

explanation: Primary healthcare is the first level of contact individuals have with the national health system, focusing on community-level promotion and prevention. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T8#BMP110_U1_T8_h3)

question: Who must officially confirm and certify death before last offices can begin?

options.A: The mortuary attendant
options.B: A registered midwife
options.C: A qualified medical doctor
options.D: The head of the nursing unit

explanation: Legal confirmation of death must always be carried out by a physician before nurses or midwives begin post-mortem care. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T5#BMP120_U5_T5_h1)

question: Which type of drug name is controlled directly by the pharmaceutical company that makes it?

options.A: International non-proprietary name
options.B: Generic name
options.C: Proprietary name
options.D: Chemical name

explanation: Commercial manufacturers create and trademark proprietary names to market their specific products. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T2#BMP124_U1_T2_h5)

question: How does frequent suckling at the breast prevent pregnancy during the postpartum period?

options.A: It causes the uterine lining to shed continuously
options.B: It permanently damages immature ovarian follicles
options.C: It thickens the cervical mucus to trap all bacteria
options.D: It suppresses hormones that stimulate the release of eggs

explanation: Nipple stimulation blocks the brain signals that trigger ovulation, keeping the woman naturally infertile temporarily. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T6#BMP126_U2_T6_h7)

question: Why is regular mouth care especially important for unconscious patients?

options.A: To prevent bacteria from traveling down into the lungs
options.B: To ensure the patient can speak clearly immediately
options.C: To replace the need for intravenous fluid therapy
options.D: To stimulate rapid hair growth on the head

explanation: Unconscious clients are at risk of breathing things into their airway, so keeping the mouth clean prevents oral bacteria from entering the lungs. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T1#BMP110_U5_T1_h5)

question: Why should you scrape out a bee stinger with a flat card instead of pulling it with tweezers?

options.A: Tweezers can squeeze the attached venom sac and inject more poison.
options.B: Scraping removes the entire underlying sweat gland safely.
options.C: Scraping is the only way to kill the remaining bacteria on the skin.
options.D: Tweezers will permanently stain the skin around the sting site.

explanation: Pinching the venom sac with tweezers pushes more toxin into the skin, making the reaction worse. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T7#BMP110_U7_T7_h3)

question: Why does heavy bleeding continue when tissue stays in the uterus?

options.A: The placenta continues to produce high amounts of progesterone actively
options.B: Retained products cause a sudden drop in the woman's blood pressure
options.C: The remaining tissue stops the uterine muscle fibers from contracting tightly
options.D: Incomplete tissue loss triggers an immediate allergic reaction in the cervix

explanation: The uterus needs to contract firmly to seal off bleeding blood vessels, but trapped tissue prevents these muscles from closing properly. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T3#BMP221_U1_T3_h1)

question: What is the main job of the kidneys in the body?

options.A: Maintaining fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base balance
options.B: Storing waste products until active labor begins
options.C: Regulating body temperature during the postpartum period
options.D: Producing red blood cells for fetal oxygenation

explanation: The kidneys filter blood and manage water and salt levels to keep the body's internal environment stable. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T1#BMP216_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the main difference between hearing and active listening?

options.A: Hearing only happens when a stethoscope is used
options.B: Hearing requires the patient to speak very loudly
options.C: Active listening is only done by senior medical doctors
options.D: Active listening requires conscious attention and engagement

explanation: Hearing is automatic sound perception, whereas active listening is a deliberate effort to comprehend, evaluate, and respond to the speaker. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T2#BMP110_U3_T2_h4)

question: During a speculum exam, why do midwives perform a whiff test using 10 percent potassium hydroxide?

options.A: To stain the bacterial cell walls for easy microscopic counting
options.B: To measure the exact acidity level of the vaginal walls
options.C: To kill off unwanted parasites before collecting laboratory samples
options.D: To release volatile amines that produce a distinct fishy odor

explanation: Potassium hydroxide reacts with the chemical byproducts of bacterial overgrowth, releasing a strong fishy smell that helps confirm bacterial vaginosis. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T1#BMP310_U2_T1_h5)

question: How does chronic uncontrolled hypertension damage the kidneys?

options.A: By harming the small blood vessels inside the renal tissue
options.B: By causing painful kidney stones to form rapidly
options.C: By blocking the bladder from emptying completely
options.D: By producing excessive amounts of dilute urine daily

explanation: High pressure damages the delicate blood vessels in the kidneys, reducing their ability to filter waste properly. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T2#BMP125_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the term for excessive dark hair growth in women following a male distribution pattern?

options.A: Tinea capitis
options.B: Hirsutism
options.C: Pediculosis
options.D: Alopecia

explanation: Hirsutism describes male-pattern hair growth in females, typically linked to elevated androgen hormone levels. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T8#BMP111_U4_T8_h4)

question: What is usually the main source of systemic fluoride for communities?

options.A: Drinking water supplies
options.B: Imported citrus fruits
options.C: Processed dairy products
options.D: Fresh green leafy vegetables

explanation: Public drinking water is commonly the main way people get fluoride in their daily diet. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T12#BMP118_U2_T12_h5)

question: What action helps reduce risks when transferring a client from a primary clinic to a general hospital?

options.A: Providing clear referral notes and effective handover communication
options.B: Allowing the client to travel without any documentation
options.C: Encouraging the family to bypass hospital registration
options.D: Withholding clinical history until the patient recovers fully

explanation: Clear notes and handovers ensure the receiving facility understands the clinical history and urgency of the case. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T5#BMP110_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why is nephrotic syndrome best described as a collection of clinical findings rather than just one disease?

options.A: It changes its symptoms completely every few days.
options.B: It only affects adults with multiple chronic illnesses.
options.C: It cannot be diagnosed using standard laboratory tests.
options.D: It can be triggered by several different underlying health conditions that damage the kidneys.

explanation: Nephrotic syndrome groups together signs like heavy protein loss and swelling that happen when various conditions damage the kidneys. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T5#BMP216_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical pharmacokinetic change seen during pregnancy?

options.A: Altered liver enzyme activity
options.B: Increased renal clearance
options.C: Decreased total body water volume
options.D: Elevated plasma volume

explanation: Total body water actually increases substantially during pregnancy, rather than decreasing. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T4#BMP124_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which of the following practices is NOT recommended when protecting a community well or borehole?

options.A: Allowing community members to dip their personal fetching buckets directly into the well
options.B: Ensuring the surrounding soil is free from pit latrines and soakaway pits
options.C: Constructing a perimeter fence to keep roaming livestock at a safe distance
options.D: Building drainage channels to carry spilled water away from the head

explanation: Dipping personal buckets introduces outside germs into the clean water source; closed pumps or spouts are much safer. [learn more](BMP117_U4_T1#BMP117_U4_T1_h3)

question: What causes the sudden rise in prolactin that brings in milk after childbirth?

options.A: The closure of the fetal ductus arteriosus
options.B: The sudden increase in maternal body temperature
options.C: The first bath given to the newborn baby
options.D: The delivery of the placenta and drop in progesterone

explanation: During pregnancy, progesterone blocks milk production. Once the placenta is delivered, progesterone drops, allowing prolactin to do its job. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T2#BMP218_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why is it dangerous to recap used needles after a medical procedure?

options.A: It makes the needle too blunt to use on the next patient
options.B: It exposes the sterile medication inside to room air
options.C: Hospital administrative policies forbid keeping needles in trays
options.D: It greatly increases the risk of accidental needle-stick injuries

explanation: Trying to guide a cap back onto a used needle often results in piercing your own finger, exposing you to blood-borne infections. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T3#BMP120_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why is a plenary debriefing session essential at the end of small group work?

options.A: It prevents students from leaving with incorrect clinical assumptions.
options.B: It proves that group work is superior to clinical ward placements.
options.C: It gives the educator an excuse to hand out a surprise written quiz.
options.D: It takes up the remaining time so the educator can leave early.

explanation: Summarizing findings allows the educator to correct misconceptions and consolidate the learning points for everyone. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T7#BMP312_U3_T7_h6)

question: What is the medical term for having a lower than normal number of platelets?

options.A: Thrombocytosis
options.B: Leukopenia
options.C: Thrombocytopenia
options.D: Erythrocytosis

explanation: Thrombocytopenia means low platelets, which can increase the risk of bleeding and easy bruising. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T4#BMP111_U5_T4_h6)

question: Which gland releases gonadotropin-releasing hormone into the body?

options.A: Hypothalamus
options.B: Adrenal gland
options.C: Ovarian cortex
options.D: Anterior pituitary gland

explanation: The hypothalamus is the specialized brain structure responsible for pulsing out gonadotropin-releasing hormone to direct the pituitary gland. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T4#BMP210_U2_T4_h1)

question: When old red blood cells are broken down, what happens to the salvaged iron?

options.A: It is permanently stored inside the white blood cells
options.B: It is transported back to the bone marrow to make new cells
options.C: It is excreted immediately through the kidneys in urine
options.D: It is converted into bilirubin and eliminated in the stool

explanation: The body carefully conserves iron, binding it to transferrin and returning it to the bone marrow for the production of new erythrocytes. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T2#BMP111_U5_T2_h5)

question: Which strategy is NOT recommended when counseling a patient about preventing future episodes of trichomoniasis?

options.A: Relying solely on herbal vaginal douches after intercourse
options.B: Using barrier methods like condoms consistently during sex
options.C: Ensuring sexual partners are treated at the same time
options.D: Seeking prompt medical care if abnormal symptoms return

explanation: Vaginal douching does not cure trichomoniasis and can actually push the infection higher into the reproductive tract or disrupt healthy flora. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T7#BMP310_U2_T7_h6)

question: What happens in the liver during disease that leads to portal hypertension and ascites?

options.A: Fibrotic scar tissue blocking blood flow
options.B: Excessive production of red blood cells
options.C: Rapid regeneration of healthy liver tissue
options.D: Infection of the gallbladder by bacteria

explanation: Scar tissue in a diseased liver physically blocks blood from flowing through the portal system, raising the pressure inside those blood vessels. [learn more](BMP125_U4_T6#BMP125_U4_T6_h1)

question: Where does the lymphatic fluid from the uterine fundus primarily drain?

options.A: Superficial femoral nodes
options.B: Inguinal lymph nodes
options.C: Axillary lymph nodes
options.D: Lumbar lymph nodes

explanation: Lymphatics from the upper fundus travel upward with the ovarian vessels to drain into the lumbar or aortic lymph nodes. [learn more](BMP210_U2_T3#BMP210_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the term for the entire group of people a researcher wants to study?

options.A: Control cohort
options.B: Pilot group
options.C: Research sample
options.D: Target population

explanation: The target population is the complete group of individuals the researcher is interested in and wants to apply their findings to. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T7#BMP225_U2_T7_h1)
